gloss: sorry to keep you waiting; thanks for waiting

definitions.gloss: sorry to keep you waiting; thanks for waiting
definitions.explanation: A set phrase used when arriving late or when someone has been waiting for you. Also used by service staff when bringing food or completing a task.

examples.japanese: お{待|ま}たせ！{遅|おく}れてごめん。
examples.english: Sorry for the wait! Sorry I'm late.

examples.japanese: お{待|ま}たせしました。ご{注文|ちゅうもん}の{品|しな}です。
examples.english: Thank you for waiting. Here is your order.

examples.japanese: {大変|たいへん}お{待|ま}たせいたしました。ただいまお{席|せき}にご{案内|あんない}いたします。
examples.english: I'm very sorry to have kept you waiting. I will show you to your seat now.

notes:
Shortened form of お{待|ま}たせしました. The casual form お{待|ま}たせ is used between friends and family, while お{待|ま}たせしました is standard polite, and {大変|たいへん}お{待|ま}たせいたしました is humble/formal.

POLITENESS LEVELS:
- お{待|ま}たせ: casual, among friends
- お{待|ま}たせしました: standard polite, used in shops and restaurants
- {大変|たいへん}お{待|ま}たせいたしました: very formal, used in business or upscale service

USAGE:
Used in two main contexts:
- When you arrive and someone has been waiting for you
- When service staff deliver something to a customer (food, documents, etc.)

The phrase is almost automatic in service contexts. Even if the wait was very short, staff will say お{待|ま}たせしました as a courtesy.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {遅|おく}れてすみません: sorry for being late — a direct apology for lateness, not used in service contexts
- お{待|ま}ちください: please wait — the requesting side, not the apologizing side
